pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions | The House of Suntory
pages.description: Suntory's answers on its spirits, its history and visits to the Yamazaki and Hakushu distilleries.
pages.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

What is the brief history of Japanese whisky?
The House of Suntory is present in every stage of Japanese whisky history. Its founder, Shinjiro Torii, learned about Western spirits from a young age and mastered blending. His passion led him to found Japan's first whisky distillery, the Yamazaki Distillery, in 1923, and to release the first whisky made in Japan to the market in 1929. Suntory Shirofuda was not a great commercial success, but it taught him how to suit the Japanese palate. He achieved this in 1937 with Suntory Whisky Kakubin, still Japan's top-selling whisky (IWSR 2022). Japanese whisky began to gain international recognition in the 1980s.

Who is the Japanese whisky creator?
Nicknamed the "Nose of Osaka," Shinjiro Torii paved the way by establishing Japan's first whisky distillery, Yamazaki, in 1923.

When did gin first come to Japan?
In the 19th century. In 1936 the House of Suntory introduced Hermes Dry-Gin, and Roku Gin launched worldwide in 2016.

Do the Yamazaki and Hakushu distillery tours include tastings?
Yes. Tours are booked by lottery; reservations usually open on the first business day two months before the tour date, and tours last 80 to 90 minutes on average. Yamazaki Distillery: +81-75-962-14-23.

Are Yamazaki whiskies your most awarded?
Yes, with approximately 91 awards and recognitions in the last 10 years.

pages.title: Yamazaki distillery - Wikipedia
pages.description: Encyclopedia entry on the Yamazaki distillery in Shimamoto, Osaka Prefecture.
pages.text:
Yamazaki distillery (山崎蒸溜所) is a Japanese whisky distillery in Shimamoto, Osaka Prefecture, Japan. Owner: Suntory. Founded: 1923. Founder: Shinjirō Torii. Stills: 6 wash stills, 6 spirit stills. Opened in 1923 and owned by Suntory, it was Japan's first commercial whisky distillery. Seven thousand bottles of unblended malt whisky are on display in its "Whisky Library".

History
The Yamazaki distillery was opened in 1923 by Shinjirō Torii as the first malt whisky distillery in Japan. Torii, founder and chairman of Kotobukiya (the predecessor company of Suntory), hired Taketsuru Masataka and made him factory director of the Yamazaki distillery in 1924. Taketsuru had been in Scotland in 1918, studied at Glasgow University, and came to Japan in 1920 with his Scottish wife, Rita Cowan. Under Taketsuru the first whisky was completed in 1929 and sold as Shirofuda (white label). After differences with Torii, Taketsuru left the company in 1934 and founded Dai-Nippon Kaju KK, later Nikka Whisky Distilling, in Hokkaidō the same year.

Evaluation
The 18-Year earned six consecutive double gold medals at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition between 2008 and 2013. Yamazaki 25 Year Old was named Best Japanese Single Malt at the 2013 World Whisky Awards, and Jim Murray's Whisky Bible 2015 named Yamazaki Single Malt Sherry Cask 2013 World Whisky of the Year.

Categories: Suntory; Japanese whisky; Japanese companies established in 1923; Shimamoto, Osaka

pages.title: History - Suntory Yamazaki Distillery
pages.description: Difford's Guide history of Suntory's Yamazaki distillery near Kyoto.
pages.text:
Suntory Yamazaki Distillery. Status: Operational. Established: 1924. Owner: Suntory Global Spirits. Visitor Policy: Not generally accessible.

Yamazaki, Japan's first malt whisky distillery, was completed in 1924.

Masataka Taketsuru, from a family of sake brewers, studied applied chemistry at Glasgow University and worked in Scotch distilleries, returning home in 1920 with his Scottish bride, Rita. Shinjiro Torii founded his Suntory Company in 1899 and made a fortune selling Akadama Port Wine. Torii paid for the distillery, and Taketsuru agreed to work for him for ten years before leaving to found his own distillery, Nikka.

Torii started building Yamazaki in 1923 on the outskirts of Kyoto, in a narrow valley between Mt. Tennozan and Mt. Otokoyama, where the Katsura, Uji and Kizu rivers meet the Yodo. The site was chosen for its water.

Production started the next year, and Taketsuru made the first brand, Suntory Shirofuda (White Label), in 1929. It was too smoky for Japanese drinkers, but gave Suntory time to build stocks for the lighter Kakubin blend in 1937. Extra malt was added to Kakubin in 1989. By the 1970s Torii's second son, Keizo Saji, ran the company, and in 1984 Yamazaki single malt whisky was launched.

Suntory Yamazaki 12 Year Old: launched in 1984, Japan's best-selling single malt.
Yamazaki Sherry Cask: the first cask stored at the Yamazaki soon after distilling started there in 1923 was a 480 litre Spanish oak Oloroso butt.
Suntory Yamazaki 18 year old: launched in 1992.

pages.title: Yamazaki Distillery: a brand history - The Spirits Business
pages.description: Trade press history of Suntory's Yamazaki distillery and its whiskies.
pages.text:
Yamazaki Distillery: a brand history
25 April 2017, by Amy Hopkins

Established by Shinjiro Torii, founder of Japanese drinks group Suntory, Yamazaki became Japan's first whisky distillery in 1923. It is at the foot of Mt. Tenno in Shimamoto, Osaka. In 1899, aged 20, Torii founded Torii Shoten in Osaka and began making wine.

Torii became Yamazaki's first master blender. The distillery started distilling in 1924 and released its first product, Suntory Whisky 'Shirofuda' (White Label), in 1929. In 1961 Torii's son Keizo Saji became Suntory's second president and Yamazaki's second master blender; he oversaw the building of the Hakushu and Chita distilleries in the 1970s. Saji led the move into single malt in 1984 with Suntory Single Malt Whisky Yamazaki, followed by Yamazaki 18 Years Old in 1992.

Heavy investment in the late 1980s, completed in 1989, let Yamazaki make a variety of malt whisky styles using multiple still designs. The distillery expanded again in 2013 with the addition of four stills, bringing its total to 12 and raising capacity by roughly 40%. The following year Suntory bought US-based Beam Inc for US$16bn, creating Beam Suntory.

Jim Murray named Yamazaki Sherry Cask 2013 World Whisky of the Year in his Whisky Bible 2015. It launched at about US$120 and can now cost US$4,000.

Timeline: 1879 Shinjiro Torii born. 1923 Yamazaki Distillery built in Shimamoto, Osaka Prefecture. 1929 Suntory Whisky 'White Label'. 1984 Suntory Single Malt Whisky Yamazaki. 2013 Suntory invests US$50m to ramp up Yamazaki's capacity. March 2014 Yamazaki Distiller's Reserve launches.

expected.notes: opened 1923: the official House of Suntory page (founded the Yamazaki Distillery in 1923; established Yamazaki in 1923), Wikipedia (opened in 1923; Founded: 1923) and The Spirits Business (Japan's first whisky distillery in 1923; the 1923 timeline entry). Difford's Guide gives 1924, but official over reference and three pages over one make 1923 the stored value.

notes: Conflicts: (1) The founding: 1923 on the official page, Wikipedia and The Spirits Business; Difford's Guide says Established: 1924 and completed in 1924, though it also says Torii started building in 1923. The official 1923 should win, with Difford's Guide cited for 1924 if kept. (2) The first distilling: The Spirits Business says 1924, and Difford's Guide says production started the next year after 1923 but also that distilling started there in 1923; Difford's Guide therefore supports neither, and a generic 1924 event is optional. Wikipedia makes Taketsuru factory director in 1924. (3) Torii's firm: Difford's Guide says he founded his Suntory Company in 1899; The Spirits Business says he founded Torii Shoten in 1899; Wikipedia calls the predecessor Kotobukiya. The 1899 date is the company's, not the distillery's, and must not become an opened event. Traps: Suntory's 2014 purchase of Beam changed the parent group, not Yamazaki's owner, so it is not an acquired event for Yamazaki. The 1929 Shirofuda, 1937 Kakubin and its 1989 recipe change, the 1984 single malt, the 1992 18 Year Old, the 2014 Distiller's Reserve and the 1936 and 2016 gins are bottle launches, not distillery events. The Whisky Bible title, the medals, the award counts, the US$120 and US$4,000 prices, the tour lottery and the phone number must be left out. Hakushu and Chita are other distilleries. Stills: Wikipedia gives 6 wash and 6 spirit stills, which matches the 12 stills The Spirits Business reports after 2013; capacity is not given in litres of alcohol. No suntory.com page is included: the factory page and the Suntory news release returned no text, so the House of Suntory FAQ is the official source. Peated stores the owner Suntory Global Spirits and suntory.com/factory/yamazaki as website. Page texts are reviewed paraphrases of the cited pages, not copies. Generic events are allowed but never required, so these are not expected: generic 1989, the late-1980s investment completed, and generic 2013, four stills added (both from The Spirits Business only).
